intro: The short version of the record below: what I was working on, when, and what each stage taught me. Each chapter opens the milestones behind it.

chapters.title: Security before software
chapters.story: I started by taking networks apart to see how they behaved, long before I had a job title. While still at school I carried out a formal vulnerability assessment and had to explain the findings to the people who owned the system.
chapters.learned: Watching how systems fail is the fastest way to learn how they work, and a finding only matters if you can explain it.

chapters.title: Learning by running everything
chapters.story: I studied computer science while already shipping .NET and PHP e-commerce work. At PureLogics I moved from senior engineer to co-partner and CTO, and the job grew to include VMware, Asterisk telephony, Cisco networks and a Facebook-integrated application.
chapters.learned: The application is one layer. Networks, telephony and virtualisation are part of shipping, not someone else's problem.

chapters.title: A founder who kept writing code
chapters.story: I founded Xoho Tech and grew it to around 40 people across Pakistan and the United States over nine years, while still writing code, designing systems and running delivery. We adopted AWS in 2013 and built archive, media, e-signature and monitoring platforms. When power cuts kept costing developers their work, I moved development into the browser: templated workspaces that slept when idle and woke on request, later on Firecracker microVMs, with a hyperconverged lab at home to learn the layers underneath.
chapters.learned: When something keeps failing, change the system rather than asking people to work around it. Developer environments are infrastructure too.

chapters.title: AI before it was the job
chapters.story: I received access to OpenAI's private API beta on 4 June 2021, before ChatGPT. After moving to Melbourne into AWS consulting, I proposed in June 2023 a workflow where a task spins up a fresh environment and an AI prepares a plan and first changes before an engineer takes over. That October I built a multi-role AutoGen prototype and started running small, domain-specific models on my own hardware.
chapters.learned: Models are most useful inside a workflow that keeps a visible plan, a record of actions and a person verifying the result.

chapters.title: From prototypes to sensitive production
chapters.story: I ran local fine-tuning, synthetic-data and quantisation loops, and explored policy-as-code with Cedar. I earned AWS Solutions Architect Professional in July 2024, then led engineering for a clinical GenAI product, where outputs had to cite their source and every prompt change had to be measured.
chapters.learned: In sensitive domains, provenance and evaluation matter more than fluent output.

chapters.title: Applied AI at scale, and owning the compute
chapters.story: At Commonwealth Bank I work in AI Acceleration on taking AI applications from early design to production, with a focus on identity, authorisation and security evaluation, and I'm the squad's Security Champion. On my own hardware I research how small models learn to reason, using reinforcement learning, LoRA and model-inspection tools on Apple Silicon.
chapters.learned: If you adapt a model, measure what the adaptation changed, not just whether the score went up.

chapters.title: Building the piece underneath
chapters.story: My recent work goes a layer below the tools I use: AgentRC for declaring what an agent may do, agentic-agile for test-gated agent workflows, agent-handoff for carrying decisions between sessions, a JuiceFS fork for storage behaviour, and a Linux traffic-control fix merged upstream in OpenWrt.
chapters.learned: Separate what should survive from what should be replaceable. Declaring a permission is not the same as granting it.
